title: What identity data does the EU AML Regulation (AMLR) require, and can one eID provide it all? | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: AMLR Article 22(1) customer data compared with what a notified eID and the EUDI Wallet PID return, and 4 ways to complete the missing data.
body_markdown:
*The customer data Article 22(1) of the EU AML Regulation requires, what a single eID or the EUDI Wallet returns and how to fill the gaps.*


For a customer who is a natural person, Article 22(1) of the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR) requires, except in cases of lower risk, all names and surnames, place and full date of birth, nationalities and, where applicable, the national identification number, the usual place of residence and, where available, the tax identification number. One eID or the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet) often does not return all of it: the address is optional in both the eIDAS minimum data set and the wallet's person identification data.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Florentyna Frend (Head of Product), Authologic.*
